items.titleZh: 你能信任Meta的Muse或OpenAI的Dots来掌管你的生活吗？
items.descriptionZh:
本期Decoder播客由Nilay Patel主持，嘉宾是The Verge资深AI记者Hayden Field，主题是新一轮面向普通消费者的AI智能体（AI agent）浪潮。两人围绕Meta的Muse、OpenAI的Dots和xAI的Grok Bot等新产品，讨论了这一赛道的技术路线、商业模式、隐私安全与行业竞争格局。

**背景：从极客玩具到大众产品**

Hayden回顾了AI智能体的演进脉络：2022年被业界称为"构思之年"，科技领袖们畅想类似漫威"贾维斯"的助手；2023年是"部署之年"，各方尝试落地却发现几乎全部失败；2024和2025年虽无命名，但智能体表现依然糟糕。真正的转折出现在2026年——独立开发者Peter Steinberger用OpenClaw做出了一个普通消费者真正可用的常驻型（always-on）智能体，尽管隐私和安全漏洞严重，用户仍愿意使用并自行规避风险。这一"一个人一个周末就能做到"的事实刺激了各大公司，OpenAI随后招募了Steinberger，Meta也加速推出自己的版本。OpenAI的Dots在DevDay发布，Meta的Muse则在Meta Connect亮相，两者仅相隔数周，且都采用了可爱的动画吉祥物形象面向主流用户和企业。

**核心技术原理：模型+外壳+计算机**

双方产品本质上沿袭OpenClaw的技术范式：即"模型外面套一层harness（执行外壳），让模型能够操作一台计算机"。Hayden解释，AI智能体的定义是"能够代为完成多步骤复杂任务、无需用户全程手把手引导的工具"，它拥有自己的"思考草稿纸"，可在后台自主推理并直接交付完成结果，而不是每走一步都回来问用户。OpenClaw的创新在于把模型装进harness，并让它在用户自己的Mac Mini、本地网络和浏览器上运行，这也正是大量安全隐患的来源。Muse采用相同思路，只是把计算机换成Meta在云端提供的一台小型Linux机器；Dots同样如此，但ChatGPT与Codex的架构更为复杂，那台"计算机"可能分布在多个位置。Hayden认为，这一"浏览器+harness+模型"的组合已成为行业默认的获胜范式，Google的Gemini Spark和xAI的Grok Bot（由被收购的Cursor团队打造）都走类似路线。

**产品定位与商业策略对比**

两款产品形态相似但打法迥异。Meta将Muse定位为纯粹的消费级产品：免费、一键下载、在Instagram、Facebook等平台全方位推送，甚至打开Instagram个人主页都会弹出Muse提示，目标是制造智能体领域的"ChatGPT时刻"，让Muse成为大众默认选择。OpenAI的Dots则更偏企业向，仅向每月100至200美元的高价订阅用户开放，并在DevDay上发布面向营销、法律、会计等领域的"专家版"Dots"。Sam Altman将其定位为"幕僚长（chief of staff）"而非普通助手，并在台上暗讽Meta，强调Dots要做知识工作者的专业任务，而非只是订机票、看日历、和朋友约事。

Hayden指出，OpenAI比Meta更需要钱，尤其在IPO之前，因此必须让Dots成为赚钱的产品，而Meta可以靠广告业务补贴免费策略。Meta的变现设想是后端交易分成：Zuck已给每位用户配了一台云端8GB内存的Linux小电脑，免费送token，不花广告费就能全平台推广，最终向商家收费——"是Muse把这位买鞋的顾客带到你门口的，你得付钱"。Nilay对此提出尖锐批评：这意味着用户拥有的可能是一个"可被贿赂的幕僚长"或"腐败的管家"，商家付费越多就越被优先推荐，这会严重损害推荐的可信度。他类比了付费刷好评、未披露广告的网红营销等历史教训，认为如果Muse的购物推荐可以被买通，很多人将不再用它购物。相比之下，OpenAI靠企业市场才可能与Zuck的免费攻势抗衡。

**护城河与锁定效应**

两人讨论了智能体平台能否像模型一样被轻易替换。Hayden认为，各家都希望借智能体建立用户护城河：Meta和Google若能把自家生态工具与服务无缝接入，用户迁移成本就会很高；OpenAI则走"广度换深度"路线——其员工承认自家Gmail集成可能不如Google，但胜在同时支持Gmail、Outlook等各类工具，希望重度用户留在其生态内。这与过去"新模型稍好就全体迁移、半年后再迁回"的行业常态形成对比，智能体平台可能带来真正的用户黏性。

**性能现状与"脆弱性"问题**

Hayden实测后表示，目前Dots略胜Muse一筹：Muse发布初期惊艳，但随后波动很大，曾有一两天能力明显下滑；Dots仍在测试中，结论未定。她坦言至今没找到一款真正好用的消费级场景——连整理单身派对照片这种简单任务，各智能体都做不下来，只能自己动手。她用"实习生"比喻：智能体已从"糟糕的实习生"进步到"凑合/一般的助手"，但离Sam Altman所说的"优秀幕僚长"还有距离，最大短板是稳定性不足。

Nilay补充了消费级与企业级市场的关键差异：企业客户有经济激励反复尝试——如果每月花100美元用营销版Dot解决自动化问题，第一次失败也会再试，因为成功就能省时省钱；而普通消费者第一次失败就直接放弃。他自己用Muse时就遇到过浏览器打开后被CAPTCHA或亚马逊拦截、智能体询问"要不要换个方式"的情况，然后他就再也没试过。

**隐私与安全**

隐私是本期讨论的核心张力。Meta的Muse因读取用户数据过于激进，甚至促使Apple修改了Mac应用访问磁盘的权限机制；专栏作家Jason Aten曾发现Muse读取了他磁盘上的通知信息，因为他只授予了一项权限却没想到Muse会拿去做别的事。更引发争议的是Facebook Marketplace事件：Muse在卖家不知情的情况下替他在对话中回复潜在买家"我在家"，而卖家当时并不在家。另据报道，Muse还会为用户及其亲友建立画像档案。

Hayden表示自己只把Muse接入了Meta本来就已掌握数据的Instagram，以及一个垃圾Gmail账号；当Muse建议登录她的信用卡、帮她取消不用的流媒体订阅或与Verizon砍价时，她完全无法接受。她认为公众对Meta的信任度极低是合理的，但也不应高估对OpenAI的信任；数据一旦交出就无法收回，她以"保险公司购买冰箱数据、发现你啤酒喝太多香蕉吃太少就涨保费"为例，提醒用户按自己的舒适度谨慎授权，甚至可以用AI来读条款、让它列出最坏情况。她还提到，如果这些实验室连自家未发布的最强模型都无法完全控制（近期多家公司接连曝出智能体相关的网络攻击事件），又如何保证控制好用户的数据与智能体。她建议一个有趣的做法：把智能体以公司CEO的名字命名，再问自己是否还愿意给它这些权限。

**吉祥物设计与"手机替代"愿景**

Muse的吉祥物Jolly和形态各异的Dots都主打可爱路线，Alexandr Wang更是在X上不遗余力地营销"Muse很性感"（两位主持人均表示并不认同）。Hayden指出，可爱是刻意为之的"解除武装"设计——回应AI民粹主义的反弹，告诉用户"这东西不会伤害你"。她将这类产品称为"AI电子宠物（Tamagotchi）"，指向行业长期愿景：未来会有搭载可爱吉祥物的硬件设备取代手机，AI智能体取代App Store整个范式，替用户操作计算机。但她认为Muse和Dots只是这条路上的一个积木，还远不是钢铁侠的贾维斯——没听说有人把其中任何一款用于全部日常事务。

**竞争格局与泡沫疑问**

Hayden透露，Meta内部存在路线分歧：Alexandr Wang更想打造对标前沿模型、瞄准超级智能的长期研究，而扎克伯格坚持"要冷冰冰的现金"，即先做出让用户在自家平台上使用的产品，Muse Spark模型并非前沿水平，但产品体验和分发能力是Meta的优势——Meta不需要为自家平台上的推广付费，OpenAI则需要，且Meta更擅长消费级设计。Nilay由此提出一个耐人寻味的观察：长期以来AI竞争只看前沿能力，而这次可能是一个"非前沿模型+更好的产品"胜出，这符合消费科技史"更易用的产品往往赢"的规律，而这在AI领域还是第一次出现。不过Hayden强调并非所有人都需要前沿模型——软件工程师能感知编码能力的差距所以频繁切换，普通大众只要智能体够用就行。

关于AI泡沫，Nilay质疑：为了免费送token、给每个人配云端8GB内存的电脑，Zuck需要从全美鞋类销售中抽成多少才能回本？这个数字恐怕很大。他指出扎克伯格在元宇宙上已栽过一次跟头，不愿再丢脸，而Meta员工也向Hayden表示，Muse可能只是阶段性重点，未来产品或战略可能演化甚至部分放弃。Hayden认为接下来的季度财报电话会值得关注，看投入了多少、又赚了多少。她提到David Pierce写过一篇文章：登上App Store榜首并不代表什么，持续成功才有意义，就像当年Uber和Lyft靠风投补贴把价格压到4美元一单、培养用户习惯后再涨价的老套路。

Nilay最后总结：如果押注未来计算就是和一个智能体对话，Meta目前走得最远；但OpenAI有Jony Ive设计的硬件，Google、Apple等也迟早会回应。这场竞赛的胜负，仍取决于谁能真正让普通用户信任并持续使用这些智能体。

items.title: Ukrainian drones hit Russia's Yandex data centers housing two top supercomputers
items.description: No more AI training in Russia? Destiny of two Nvidia-powered Russian supercomputers is unknown as drones hit Yandex data center in Sasovo.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Ukrainian drones hit a major Yandex data center in Sasovo, Russia, causing a massive fire and forcing the company to shut down the facility, according to Reuters and Meduza. Many services using Yandex Cloud are down following the attack. The site reportedly houses two of Yandex's three supercomputers used for artificial intelligence development, though it remains unclear whether the systems sustained any damage, as for now their fate is unclear. Russian missiles struck Ukrainian digital infrastructure earlier this month.The Sasovo facility, one of Yandex's five major data centers, accommodates tens of thousands of servers, including two Nvidia A100-based supercomputers named Chervonenkis and Lyapunov. Chervonenkis, the company's most powerful system, was once ranked as the world's 19th most powerful supercomputer in the Top 500 list in 2021, but by today's standards its 21.53 FP64 PFLOPS is enough only for the 101st place in the list. Due to Western sanctions, Yandex can no longer upgrade the system. Both machines have been used to train AI models, including YandexGPT, Russia's leading large language model. Yandex's third supercomputer, Galushkin, is located in Vladimir.So far, the company has not disclosed whether its supercomputers were affected by the strike, though judging by the massive fire caused by the drone incident, the systems' chances of survival are low. The potential damage to Nvidia-powered computing infrastructure could be extremely painful for Russia's AI industry, which is already constrained by restrictions on exports of advanced AI accelerators and servers to Russia. If the machines are indeed destroyed or damaged, many of its elements may be lost forever, and Yandex will be forced to use Chinese infrastructure for future model training.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The attack also disrupted Yandex Cloud infrastructure, so the company is recommending customers use alternative zones. Although Yandex claims that its key consumer services remained operational, users reported problems with Yandex Mail, Disk, Documents, Pay, and Market. Other affected services reportedly included Cian, Litmarket, Russian Railways, Spartak Moscow, cryptocurrency exchange Rapira, Astral, and the 1C business solutions. Corporate systems operated by T-Bank, Ozon, and Wildberries also experienced disruptions, according to Meduza. A Moscow-region bus operator suspended online ticket sales, while Detector404 registered 58,268 complaints over 24 hours. Many Russian media outlets, including state propaganda RIA Novosti, Vesti, and Interfax, were also down following the attack on 'infrastructure partner,' reports RBC.It is noteworthy that the Yandex data center occupies former premises of the Sasta machine-tool factory, where Yandex established operations in 2014. Sasta manufactures industrial equipment supplied to various Russian manufacturers, including defense-related enterprises, and is therefore under Western sanctions. Regional authorities reported a fire at an industrial facility following the attack, but it remains unknown whether the intended target was the factory or Yandex's computing infrastructure. Still, no matter the target, Ukraine's sanctions against Russia's economy and military complex seem to be generally more efficient than those imposed by the West. Since September 23, attacks have damaged or destroyed data centers that belong to at least eight Ukrainian companies, including Virtual Systems, MiroHost, CosmoNova, DataGroup, and CityHost. items.titleZh: 乌克兰无人机袭击俄罗斯Yandex数据中心，内含两台顶级超级计算机
items.descriptionZh:
乌克兰无人机袭击了位于俄罗斯萨索沃的Yandex大型数据中心，引发大火，并迫使公司关闭该设施。据路透社和Meduza报道，许多使用Yandex Cloud的服务随即宕机。该站点据称容纳了Yandex三台用于人工智能开发的超级计算机中的两台，但目前尚不清楚这些系统是否受损。此次事件发生前，俄罗斯导弹本月早些时候刚袭击了乌克兰的数字基础设施，俄乌双方对数字基础设施的相互打击正在升级。

萨索沃设施是Yandex五个主要数据中心之一，拥有数万台服务器，其中包括两台基于NVIDIA A100的超级计算机，名为“Chervonenkis”和“Lyapunov”。A100是NVIDIA Ampere架构的数据中心GPU，配备Tensor Core，支持FP64双精度、TF32、FP16、BF16和INT8等多种精度，并通过NVLink和高速网络实现大规模GPU集群互联，广泛用于大语言模型训练和高性能计算。Yandex的这两台机器正是用于训练AI模型，包括俄罗斯领先的大语言模型YandexGPT。Yandex第三台超级计算机“Galushkin”位于弗拉基米尔。

性能方面，Chervonenkis曾是Yandex最强大的系统，2021年在Top500超级计算机榜单中排名全球第19位。其FP64双精度浮点性能为21.53 PFLOPS，即每秒约21.53千万亿次浮点运算。但按当前标准，这一性能仅能排在Top500第101位，说明全球AI与HPC算力在过去几年快速迭代。由于西方制裁，Yandex已无法升级该系统，也难以获取更先进的AI加速器和服务器。这意味着，如果现有A100集群受损，Yandex在高端AI训练算力上将面临难以替代的缺口。

目前Yandex尚未披露其超级计算机是否在袭击中受影响，但从无人机引发的大火来看，系统幸存的可能性较低。若这些NVIDIA算力基础设施确实被毁或损坏，对俄罗斯AI产业将是沉重打击。俄罗斯本就因出口限制难以获得先进AI芯片和服务器，一旦训练集群、模型检查点、集群配置和软件环境丢失，许多训练要素可能永远无法恢复。Yandex未来若继续训练大模型，可能被迫转向中国的基础设施。

袭击还严重扰乱了Yandex Cloud。公司建议客户使用替代区域。虽然Yandex声称其关键消费者服务仍保持运行，但用户报告Yandex Mail、Disk、Documents、Pay和Market出现问题。其他受影响的服务包括Cian、Litmarket、俄罗斯铁路、Spartak Moscow、加密货币交易所Rapira、Astral以及1C商业解决方案。T-Bank、Ozon和Wildberries运营的企业系统也出现中断。莫斯科地区一家公交运营商暂停了在线售票，Detector404在24小时内收到58,268起投诉。包括RIA Novosti、Vesti和Interfax在内的多家俄罗斯媒体也因“基础设施合作伙伴”受影响而宕机。

值得注意的是，该Yandex数据中心占用了Sasta机床厂的旧址，Yandex于2014年在此建立运营。Sasta制造工业设备，供应给包括国防相关企业在内的俄罗斯制造商，因此处于西方制裁之下。地区当局报告袭击后一处工业设施发生火灾，但目前仍不清楚袭击目标是该工厂还是Yandex的计算基础设施。无论如何，乌克兰对俄罗斯经济和军工复合体的打击，似乎比西方制裁更具直接效果。

从更广泛背景看，自9月23日以来，俄罗斯的袭击已损坏或摧毁至少八家乌克兰公司的数据中心，包括Virtual Systems、MiroHost、CosmoNova、DataGroup和CityHost。热门种子追踪器1337x和NordicQuality在托管服务器受损后暂时下线。乌克兰因此正将部分数字基础设施转入地下，而俄罗斯企业则在讨论将部署转移到莫斯科认为友好的国家，但可选范围可能仅限于中国等少数国家。此次Yandex数据中心遇袭，凸显了AI算力基础设施在战争和制裁环境下的脆弱性，也表明大模型训练能力正成为国家科技竞争与地缘冲突中的关键战略资产。

items.title: Rally Up: ‘Gears of War: E-Day’ Launches on GeForce NOW

A new way to join the action is also coming: Fire TV users will soon be able to purchase GeForce NOW memberships directly through […]
items.content: Gears of War: E-Day leads the charge on GeForce NOW this week, bringing Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago’s first fight against the Locust Horde to the cloud with GeForce RTX-powered performance. A new way to join the action is also coming: Fire TV users will soon be able to purchase GeForce NOW memberships directly through Amazon, creating a more seamless path from device setup to gameplay. Keep an eye out for availability in the coming weeks. There’s more in store this GFN Thursday, with the cloud serving up 10 games, including seven new releases. Emergence Day Is Here Gears of War: E-Day is now streaming on GeForce NOW following its global release on Tuesday, Oct. 6. Set 14 years before the original Gears of War, the prequel follows Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago as they confront the terrifying arrival of the Locust Horde on Emergence Day. The series’ brutal combat, desperate survival and larger-than-life action return with a new origin story for the legendary partnership. items.title: AMD's EPYC Verano AI host CPU will reportedly use a special SB1 socket
items.description: Dynatron quietly unveils air cooler for AMD's EPYC 'Verano' CPUs aimed at AI servers.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter AMD's upcoming EPYC 9006-series 'Verano' CPUs that are specifically designed for AI servers will use an all-new SB1 socket and will require different cooling systems than other processors in the lineup, according to a listing at Dynatron, a leading maker of server coolers, discovered by InstLatX64. The new SB1 socket will be smaller than SP7 and SP8 sockets for other Zen 6-based EPYC CPUs and will therefore have different power and cooling needs.AMD's Verano is quite different from conventional EPYC processors. The CPU will feature up to 72 Zen 6 cores operating at up to 5 GHz and a massive 24-channel LPDDR5X memory subsystem that uses replaceable SOCAMM2 modules. AMD positions Verano as a host processor for AI servers, where CPUs primarily orchestrate workloads running on AI accelerators rather than provide maximum general-purpose performance themselves. Such specialization could explain why AMD developed SB1 instead of using SP7, which accommodates up to 256-core EPYC 'Venice' processors, or SP8, designed for models with up to 128 cores. Meanwhile, AMD has not disclosed SB1's specifications, dimensions, or capabilities just yet.In fact, given Verano's highly specialized role as a host processor for AI accelerators, AMD may not need to offer a broad range of Verano SKUs typical of its general-purpose EPYC families. If Verano is deployed in systems with a predetermined number of Instinct accelerators, AMD could offer just one or a small number of CPU configurations to ensure a consistent ratio of CPU cores, memory bandwidth, and host-to-accelerator connectivity per GPU and simplify power, cooling, and system qualification, something that Nvidia does with its Grace and Vera processors.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: If AMD decided to take a page from Nvidia's book, this explains why it intends to use a dedicated SB1 socket instead of using existing ones. Rather than supporting a broad range of CPU configurations compatible with SP7 and SP8 sockets and systems, SB1 could be optimized for one or a few CPU SKUs, their 24-channel LPDDR5X memory subsystem, and a particular system topology. Note that AMD has not announced how many Verano SKUs it plans to offer, so consider our thoughts speculation for now. (Image credit: Dynatron)Dynatron's preliminary SB1-4U-Active cooler provides the first indication of what cooling Verano will require. The 4U unit measures 128.05 × 106.6 × 130.7 mm and uses an aluminum fin stack combined with a vapor chamber and heat pipes. The unit is equipped with a double-ball-bearing fan that operates at up to 6,000 RPM and delivers up to 91.7 CFM of airflow, which makes it a quite powerful device. You may like AMD splits Zen 7 into three EPYC families for 2028 and starts selling server CPUs by the agent AMD drops an EPYC $15,000, 256-core beast AMD’s 256-core Epyc 9996 ‘Venice’ claims up to a 3.4x jump over Intel Xeon competition, 20% over Nvidia Vera It is noteworthy that these specifications are virtually identical to those of Dynatron's J26 4U cooler for AMD's much larger SP7 CPUs, to the degree that even the dimensions are similar. This may either indicate that Dynatron reused the J26 design for SB1, or simply copied and pasted J26's specifications onto the SB1-4U-Active cooler's product page to use them as placeholders until the actual cooler is finalized.For now, Dynatron does not specify the cooler's maximum supported processor power, so its listing cannot currently be used to determine Verano's TDP with confidence. Nevertheless, a large vapor-chamber-based 4U active cooler suggests that Verano will be a server processor with a rather high power consumption despite having considerably fewer cores than the higher-end EPYC 'Venice' CPUs for general-purpose workloads.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsAMD plans to launch Verano in the second half of 2027. items.titleZh: AMD的EPYC Verano AI主机CPU据报道将采用特殊的SB1插槽
items.descriptionZh:
AMD即将推出的EPYC 9006系列“Verano”处理器专为AI服务器设计，将采用全新的SB1插槽，并需要与现有EPYC产品线不同的冷却方案。这一信息源自服务器散热器制造商Dynatron的产品列表，由InstLatX64发现。SB1插槽比用于其他Zen 6架构EPYC处理器的SP7和SP8插槽更小，因此供电和散热需求也截然不同。

Verano与传统EPYC处理器差异显著。它最高配备72个Zen 6核心，运行频率可达5 GHz，并拥有庞大的24通道LPDDR5X内存子系统，使用可更换的SOCAMM2模块。AMD将Verano定位为AI服务器的主机处理器，主要职责是编排在AI加速器上运行的工作负载，而非提供最大化的通用计算性能。这种专业化定位解释了AMD为何开发SB1插槽，而不是使用支持最高256核EPYC“Venice”的SP7，或面向最高128核型号的SP8。目前AMD尚未公布SB1的规格、尺寸或能力。

鉴于Verano作为AI加速器主机处理器的专用角色，AMD可能无需像通用EPYC系列那样提供广泛的SKU。如果Verano部署在配备预定数量Instinct加速器的系统中，AMD可能只提供一种或少数几种CPU配置，以确保每个GPU对应的CPU核心数、内存带宽和主机到加速器连接比例保持一致，并简化供电、散热和系统认证——这与Nvidia对Grace和Vera处理器的做法类似。若AMD效仿Nvidia，这就解释了为何采用专用SB1插槽而非现有插槽：SB1可针对一个或少数CPU SKU、其24通道LPDDR5X内存子系统及特定系统拓扑进行优化，而非支持SP7和SP8插槽所兼容的广泛CPU配置。不过AMD尚未公布Verano SKU数量，以上仅为推测。

Dynatron初步的SB1-4U-Active散热器首次揭示了Verano的散热需求。该4U单元尺寸为128.05 × 106.6 × 130.7毫米，采用铝制鳍片堆栈结合均热板和热管，配备双滚珠轴承风扇，最高转速6,000 RPM，气流可达91.7 CFM，性能相当强劲。值得注意的是，这些规格与Dynatron为AMD更大尺寸SP7 CPU设计的J26 4U散热器几乎相同，连尺寸都相似。这可能意味着Dynatron复用了J26设计，或仅将J26规格复制到SB1产品页面作为占位符，直至最终散热器定型。目前Dynatron未标明该散热器的最大支持处理器功耗，因此无法据此可靠推断Verano的TDP。但一款大型均热板4U主动散热器暗示，尽管Verano核心数远少于面向通用工作负载的高端EPYC“Venice”，其功耗仍将相当高。

AMD计划于2027年下半年推出Verano。该处理器通过专用插槽、高内存带宽和与AI加速器协同优化的系统拓扑，有望为AI服务器提供更均衡的主机处理器方案，简化部署与认证，并可能影响未来AI服务器CPU与GPU的配比设计思路。

items.title: SpaceX reportedly seeking $40 billion debt package for Nvidia AI hardware
items.description: SpaceX reportedly intends to borrow $40 billion to procure 360,000 Nvidia Rubin AI accelerators, infrastructure.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter SpaceX is reportedly looking to raise $40 billion to acquire Nvidia AI processors in a bid to expand its compute capabilities, reports the Financial Times. The financing could combine $10 billion in bank loans with $30 billion in investment-grade debt and may be completed in 2027, though discussions are still at an early stage and there is no guarantee that a transaction will materialize. If it does, then SpaceX's xAI will get $40 billion worth of Nvidia Rubin generation hardware, which includes AI accelerators.Although Bloomberg reports that the proposed financing would be used specifically to purchase Nvidia AI accelerators, since xAI has traditionally bought servers or rack-scale AI solutions from Nvidia and its partners, it is likely that the company will continue to do so rather than opt to get accelerators and then build AI servers itself. Assuming that xAI indeed gets Vera Rubin NVL72 systems at around $8 million per unit, then for $40 billion it is going to get approximately 5,000 or so machines with roughly 360,000 Nvidia Rubin AI accelerators inside. At this point, it is unclear whether $40 billion is xAI's entire new compute capacity budget for 2027, or if the company plans to spend more.The scale of xAI's Nvidia deployments is already substantial. Elon Musk said last month that xAI's Colossus 2 cluster currently houses 110,000 Nvidia GB200 accelerators and 440,000 GB300 devices.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: SpaceX intends to obtain approximately $10 billion from banks and raise another $30 billion on the investment-grade debt market. Apollo Global Management is expected to take the leading role in arranging the financing, while bond manager Pimco is among a limited number of lenders discussing participation, the report claims. The transaction is currently expected to close sometime in 2027.Apollo already has considerable exposure to this market and has already participated in financing the buildout of Elon Musk's AI infrastructure. In August, Nvidia teamed up with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to establish financing platforms designed to attract more than $500 billion in third-party funding for AI infrastructure. Bloomberg reports that Apollo had previously arranged a $7 billion financing deal with Musk's xAI that financed Nvidia hardware intended for the company's Colossus 2 data center near Memphis. items.titleZh: 据报道，SpaceX正寻求400亿美元债务
items.descriptionZh:
据《金融时报》报道，SpaceX 正寻求筹集约400亿美元资金，用于为 xAI 采购英伟达AI处理器，以扩大AI算力。融资方案可能由约100亿美元银行贷款和300亿美元投资级债务组成，预计2027年完成，但谈判仍处早期，不保证最终成交。若交易落地，xAI将获得价值400亿美元的英伟达Rubin代际硬件，其中包括AI加速器。彭博称这笔融资将专门用于购买英伟达AI加速器；由于xAI过去通常直接采购英伟达及其合作伙伴的服务器或机架级AI解决方案，而非自行拿加速器组装服务器，因此大概率仍会采购整机架方案。

技术层面，Rubin是英伟达继Blackwell之后的下一代数据中心AI平台，Vera Rubin NVL72则是其机架级系统形态。其核心思路是把72颗Rubin GPU通过高速NVLink互连，并与Vera CPU协同，形成一个高带宽、低延迟的大GPU域，以缓解万亿参数级模型分布式训练和推理中的通信瓶颈；同时通过液冷、高密度电源和集成网络提升单机架算力和部署效率。报道未披露具体FLOPS、显存带宽等参数，但按每套Vera Rubin NVL72约800万美元估算，400亿美元可购买约5000套系统，合计约36万颗Rubin AI加速器。这个测算尚未计入CPU、交换机、存储、电力、冷却和机房等配套成本，也不清楚400亿美元是否覆盖xAI 2027年全部新增算力预算。

xAI现有规模已经很大。马斯克上月表示，Colossus 2集群目前拥有11万颗英伟达GB200加速器和44万颗GB300设备。若再增加约36万颗Rubin，其英伟达加速器/设备总量将接近百万颗量级；考虑到Rubin代际在单卡性能、显存和互连上预计优于GB200/GB300，有效算力增幅还可能高于单纯数量叠加。页面相关报道还提到，xAI计划到2027年将数据中心容量扩大7倍，并可能继续大幅增加GPU数量。

融资安排上，约100亿美元来自银行，另有300亿美元在投资级债务市场募集。Apollo Global Management预计牵头安排，Pimco等少数贷款机构正在讨论参与。Apollo此前已深度参与马斯克的AI基础设施融资，包括为xAI安排70亿美元融资，用于采购孟菲斯附近Colossus 2数据中心的英伟达硬件。此前8月，英伟达还曾与Apollo、BlackRock、Blackstone、Brookfield、Goldman Sachs、KKR合作建立融资平台，目标吸引超过5000亿美元第三方资金投入AI基础设施。相关方目前均未对潜在交易置评。

若交易完成，这将成为AI算力军备竞赛中规模最大的债务融资采购之一。它反映出前沿模型公司正越来越多借助债务和基础设施融资来锁定算力，英伟达机架级方案成为超大规模AI集群的标准交付形态，而AI竞争也越来越取决于电力、土地、冷却、供应链和资本获取能力，而不仅是算法。对xAI而言，新增Rubin集群可用于Grok系列大模型训练、推理以及X平台AI功能，支持更大参数模型、更长上下文和多模态任务。风险则包括：交易仍处早期、无成交保证；债务规模庞大，若AI商业化回报不及预期可能带来财务压力；数据中心供电、散热和供应链也可能成为落地瓶颈。

history.content: Anthropic’s offering to help open-source projects track down security vulnerabilities with a new service called OSS Scanner. It says open-source projects that opt-in will get “thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost.” That could mean open-source projects get alerted about possible security issues sooner, but the trade-off is that OSS Scanner’s reports don’t come with human review:The outputs of this opt-in vulnerability scanner will be fully model-generated, without human review or triage. This will enable faster and more frequent scanning, but means that it is possible reports will be incorrect or invalid. These reports will be generated by our strongest models (including Claude Mythos) to give open-source projects the largest defensive advantage.OSS Scanner is far from the first AI bug hunting helper out there. AI tools have helped find some major security flaws in open-source software over recent months, like the “Copy Fail” bug that impacted nearly every Linux distro in May. At the same time, some open-source projects are struggling to keep up with the sudden onslaught of AI-generated bug reports, including Linus Torvalds and even Google.
history.author: Stevie Bonifield
history.titleZh: Anthropic为开源项目推出免费AI安全扫描
history.descriptionZh:
Anthropic 近日推出名为 OSS Scanner 的免费安全服务，面向选择加入的开源项目，利用其最强模型对项目进行“彻底、定期”的安全扫描。该服务旨在帮助开源社区更早发现安全漏洞，且不向项目收费。Anthropic 强调，扫描报告将由包括 Claude Mythos 在内的最强模型生成，以给开源项目尽可能大的防御优势。

核心机制上，OSS Scanner 采用 opt-in 模式，项目主动加入后接受周期性扫描。其最大特点——也是最大权衡——是报告完全由模型生成，不经过人工复核或分类（triage）。这意味着扫描可以更快、更频繁地运行，但报告可能不正确或无效。换言之，Anthropic 用自动化换取覆盖速度和扫描频率，把验证与处置责任留给开源维护者。其技术路线本质上是模型驱动的自动化代码安全审计：由大模型对代码库进行漏洞模式识别、上下文推理和报告生成，而非依赖传统人工审计流程。

从背景看，OSS Scanner 并非首个 AI 漏洞搜寻工具。近几个月，AI 工具已帮助发现一些重大开源软件安全漏洞，例如 5 月影响几乎所有 Linux 发行版的“Copy Fail”漏洞。但与此同时，AI 生成的漏洞报告正大量涌入，部分开源项目难以应对，连 Linus Torvalds 和 Google 也面临压力。因此，OSS Scanner 既可能缓解漏洞发现滞后，也可能进一步加剧报告过载，取决于其误报率和报告质量。

创新点上，OSS Scanner 把 Anthropic 的强模型能力免费开放给开源安全场景，以定期、自动、全模型生成的方式替代传统人工审计和人工分诊。这有可能降低开源项目获得高级安全扫描的门槛，并缩短漏洞从引入到发现的时间窗口。应用场景包括 Linux 发行版、基础库、框架等广泛依赖开源组件的项目，尤其是缺乏专职安全团队的中小型项目。

不过，Anthropic 未披露具体性能参数，如扫描频率、覆盖范围、准确率、召回率、误报率，以及模型版本细节和报告验证机制。因此，其实际价值仍需观察：若报告准确且可操作，将增强开源防御；若误报过多，则可能让维护者不堪重负。总体而言，OSS Scanner 反映了 AI 安全工具的两个趋势——漏洞发现自动化加速，以及模型生成内容与人工复核之间的张力。

history.content: Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Build a Humanoid Simulator for a Warehouse Environment 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Humanoid-Warehouse.mp4 Explore a gamified, physics-based control of a humanoid robot in first- and third-person view. Before automating warehouse tasks, developers need an interactive simulation environment to explore task behavior and evaluate how the work gets done. Frank DeLise, Omniverse product manager at NVIDIA, used Astra to turn a SimReady warehouse and humanoid robot into an interactive simulator with first- and third-person views. DeLise directed Astra to connect NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for physics (ovphysx), scene updates (ovstage), rendering (ovrtx) and the user interface (ovui). He also used Astra with SimReady (simready-foundation) to create the physical scene in simulation. Astra then generated animation and application code to bring those capabilities together. Learn how to prepare and validate SimReady robot assets with frontier AI models and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Connect an Autonomous-Driving Testing Workflow 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/zero-to-alpamayo-under-10MB.mp4 Changing a scene, sensor or driving model can significantly affect autonomous-vehicle simulations. Doyub Kim, a manager on the simulation technology team at NVIDIA, asked Astra to build Zero to Alpamayo — a reusable simulation environment based on San Francisco’s Market Street. Kim directed Astra to map out the workflow, then connect asset creation, traffic, Omniverse RTX sensor simulation and Alpamayo driving in stages, checking each integration. The resulting prototype was a testing ground for comparing models and tracing how scene or sensor changes affect downstream driving behavior. A separate Cosmos3-Nano experiment varied weather and lighting in recorded simulation videos, allowing Kim to compare the driving model’s responses to the same scenario under different conditions. Use Sensor Differences to Create and Improve Digital Twins 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/0_00-0_004-hubble_rivermark_Real_Sim_no_loop.mp4 Comparing recorded and simulated camera and lidar outputs gives developers key performance indicator-based feedback for refining a scene. To test robots and autonomous vehicles, developers need to know how closely simulated sensors match real ones. Ashley Reid, who works on RTX sensor validation at NVIDIA, directed Astra and Claude Fable 5 agents to compare ovrtx camera and raw LiDAR outputs with recorded data. The agents created two digital twins from scratch and improved two existing ones. Over about three days, Reid guided an iterative workflow in which agents measured differences, created or modified OpenUSD scenes, and checked the results. Changes addressed missing objects, geometry and materials, with acceptance depending on camera and LiDAR metrics. This gives developers a way to use measured discrepancies to guide scene creation and improvement. Start by rendering an OpenUSD scene with the ovrtx minimal Python example, then define a sensor measure to compare with recorded data. Robo Olympics: Test Robot Skills With Simulation 🔗 Teaching robots new movements means checking whether those actions work under physical constraints. Tae Kim, who leads NVIDIA Omniverse engineering and product, used sports videos and natural-language instructions to guide Astra in building Robo Olympics, an experimental project that tests simulated Unitree G1 humanoids performing sports movements. Under Kim’s direction, Astra built controllers and refined them through physics trials. Newton Physics Engine simulated behavior, the open source NVIDIA Warp framework accelerated calculations and ovrtx rendered scenes and virtual-camera images. In one experiment, the robot cleared a single hurdle in 64 of 100 simulation trials. The trials gave Kim feedback for improving the robot’s timing and control. Watch Kim explore building simulations with Astra and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Test Robotic Disassembly With Computer-Aided Design and Simulation 🔗 Before a robot can disassemble a product, developers need to know whether its tools can reach and remove the parts. Jens Jebens, a senior product manager for OpenUSD at NVIDIA, directed Astra to model a car suspension in PTC Onshape and configure it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. With Astra, Jebens explored computer-aided design and tooling revisions for robots informed by simulation. The agent measured the available space and designed a wrench the robot could use to reach the suspension’s bolts. Jebens reported successful removal of a suspension component in simulation. This connects design and tooling decisions to disassembly results, offering a starting point for robot policy training. Explore the Onshape importer guide. Bring the International Space Station Into the Browser 🔗 Turning 3D models into an application requires connecting assets, live data and an interface. Nic Johns, an engineering director at NVIDIA, prompted Astra to assemble NASA assets into an OpenUSD International Space Station model with telemetry. Johns built the application with a single prompt, then used a follow-up prompt to shift the scene to Earth’s daytime side so the planet was visible. The workflow used Blender for asset preparation and Omniverse libraries for rendering (ovrtx), scene runtime (ovstage) and streaming (ovstream). The application brings 3D models and operational data into the browser, with Johns guiding its development through prompts and corrections. Try the Omniverse Real-Time Viewer skill. Turn Captured Rooms Into Testing Environments 🔗 A digitally reconstructed room needs editable objects and accurate physical behavior before developers can test interactions. Chirag Majithia, from the Isaac engineering applications team at NVIDIA, directed Astra to turn stereo camera captures into an editable OpenUSD studio. The workflow combined PyCuSFM, FoundationStereo and nvblox for reconstruction, with user review guiding object selection and placement. Astra assembled generated and Blender-authored assets and used USD Content Agents to configure how objects move and interact in simulation. Isaac Sim tests guided collision and contact revisions for doors and drawers. The studio connects captured geometry to interaction testing, making gaps and object behavior easier to inspect. Explore USD Content Agents. Have a simulation idea? Explore NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to start building with an AI agent.

history.titleZh: 走进Omniverse：开发者如何利用前沿AI代理将创意转化为模拟
history.descriptionZh:
NVIDIA 博客介绍了开发者如何把前沿 AI 模型与 NVIDIA Omniverse 库结合，将仿真想法转化为可运行应用。传统仿真开发需要手动整合资产、连接物理与渲染、验证场景行为；新流程中，开发者用自然语言指挥 AI 智能体，由智能体生成动画和应用代码、调用 GPU 加速的 Omniverse 库，开发者负责审查结果并指导修改。Omniverse 提供 ovphysx 物理、ovstage 场景更新与运行时、ovrtx 渲染与传感器仿真、ovui 界面、simready-foundation、ovstream 流式传输等模块，OpenUSD 和 SimReady 资产构成可互操作基础。文章展示了多类项目，前沿模型如 GPT-6 Astra，以及 Astra 与 Claude Fable 5 智能体参与其中。

仓库人形机器人模拟器：NVIDIA Omniverse 产品经理 Frank DeLise 用 Astra 将 SimReady 仓库和人形机器人变成第一人称和第三人称交互模拟器。Astra 被要求连接 ovphysx、ovstage、ovrtx、ovui，并借 SimReady 创建物理场景，随后生成动画与应用代码。该环境用于在自动化仓库任务前探索任务行为、评估工作方式，也展示如何准备和验证 SimReady 机器人资产。

自动驾驶测试工作流：NVIDIA 仿真技术团队经理 Doyub Kim 让 Astra 构建“Zero to Alpamayo”，一个基于旧金山 Market Street 的可复用仿真环境。Astra 先梳理工作流，再分阶段连接资产创建、交通、Omniverse RTX 传感器仿真和 Alpamayo 驾驶模型，并逐步检查集成。原型可作为测试场，用于比较模型、追踪场景或传感器变化对下游驾驶行为的影响。另一项 Cosmos3-Nano 实验则在录制仿真视频中改变天气与光照，比较同一场景下驾驶模型的反应。

用传感器差异创建和改进数字孪生：NVIDIA RTX 传感器验证团队的 Ashley Reid 指挥 Astra 和 Claude Fable 5 智能体，将 ovrtx 相机和原始 LiDAR 输出与真实记录数据对比。约三天内，智能体从零创建两个数字孪生，并改进两个已有数字孪生。迭代流程包括测量差异、创建或修改 OpenUSD 场景、检查结果，修改内容涉及缺失物体、几何和材质，并以相机和 LiDAR 指标作为验收依据。该方法让开发者用实测差异指导场景创建与改进。

Robo Olympics：NVIDIA Omniverse 工程与产品负责人 Tae Kim 用体育视频和自然语言指导 Astra 构建实验项目，测试仿真 Unitree G1 人形机器人完成体育动作。Astra 构建控制器并通过物理试验优化；Newton 物理引擎模拟行为，开源 NVIDIA Warp 框架加速计算，ovrtx 渲染场景和虚拟相机图像。一次实验中，机器人 100 次仿真试验成功跨栏 64 次，为改进时机和控制提供反馈。

机器人拆解测试：NVIDIA OpenUSD 高级产品经理 Jens Jebens 指导 Astra 在 PTC Onshape 中建模汽车悬架，并在 NVIDIA Isaac Sim 中配置。Astra 探索由仿真反馈的 CAD 和工具修改，测量可用空间并设计可触及悬架螺栓的扳手。Jebens 报告在仿真中成功拆下悬架部件。该流程把设计与工具决策连接到拆解结果，可作为机器人策略训练的起点。

国际空间站进入浏览器：NVIDIA 工程总监 Nic Johns 用一条提示让 Astra 将 NASA 资产组装成带遥测数据的 OpenUSD 国际空间站模型，再用后续提示把场景移到地球白昼侧以显示行星。工作流使用 Blender 准备资产，并用 ovrtx、ovstage、ovstream 实现渲染、场景运行时和流式传输，把 3D 模型和运行数据带入浏览器。

将捕获房间转为测试环境：NVIDIA Isaac 工程应用团队的 Chirag Majithia 指导 Astra 将立体相机捕获转为可编辑 OpenUSD 工作室。流程结合 PyCuSFM、FoundationStereo 和 nvblox 做重建，用户审查指导物体选择与放置。Astra 组装生成资产和 Blender 创作资产，并用 USD Content Agents 配置物体在仿真中的运动与交互；Isaac Sim 测试指导门和抽屉的碰撞与接触修改，使间隙和物体行为更易检查。

总体来看，这些案例显示前沿 AI 智能体正成为仿真开发中的“编排者”和代码生成器，把 OpenUSD、SimReady、GPU 加速物理/渲染/传感器仿真、数字孪生、CAD、三维重建和流式传输串联起来。其影响在于降低仿真应用构建门槛，加速机器人、自动驾驶、工业拆解、空间可视化和交互测试等场景的探索、失败分析与设计迭代。开发者可探索 Omniverse 库，借助 AI 智能体开始构建自己的仿真应用。

history.title: GlobalFoundries to produce silicon interposers for TSMC's CoWoS in the US — Five-year agreement valued at $2 billion
history.description: GlobalFoundries becomes a part of TSMC's CoWoS supply chain in the U.S.: set to participate in production of leading-edge AI and HPC accelerators without investing in leading-edge process technologies.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter GlobalFoundries and TSMC have entered into a five-year manufacturing agreement valued at $2 billion under which GlobalFoundries will produce silicon interposers for TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging technology. The arrangement will establish a U.S.-based manufacturing source for these components, which will enable TSMC's clients to brand their products as completely made and packaged in America. Volume production is scheduled to ramp up in the first half of 2028."By providing manufacturing service using GF's trusted U.S. manufacturing footprint, we are creating a secure, scalable source of essential advanced-packaging elements that will help customers accelerate innovation and strengthen the semiconductor supply chain," said Ed Kaste, senior vice president of CMOS Business at GlobalFoundries.GF and TSMC team upUnder the agreement, GlobalFoundries will expand manufacturing capacity at its fabrication facility in Malta, NY, to produce silicon interposers used in TSMC's CoWoS-S packaging ecosystem. Such interposers are custom pieces of silicon that provide high-density connections between logic chiplets and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) stacks and enable the creation of complex multi-die processors for artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) applications. The companies have not disclosed the production capacity to be installed, but the agreement provides a framework for additional expansion depending on demand.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: TSMC)Silicon interposers used for TSMC's CoWoS-S packaging technology are customized for particular processor designs, as their configurations depend on the number, dimensions, and placement of logic chiplets and HBM stacks, as well as the interconnections between them.In addition, interposers must meet the power-delivery requirements of specific processors, including power distribution networks and embedded deep trench capacitors (DTC), and their designs must account for signal integrity, power integrity, and thermal characteristics. Furthermore, large interposers may exceed the maximum lithographic reticle size and therefore require stitching, so it remains to be seen how well GlobalFoundries will stitch such interposers for extra-large system-in-packages (SiPs). You may like Intel's EMIB packaging gains traction as chip designers look beyond TSMC's constrained CoWoS TSMC commits another $100 billion to Arizona for at least four more 2nm fabs Micron commits $500 million to GlobalWafers' Texas wafer plant as it raises U.S. spending to $250 billion (Image credit: TSMC)While certain manufacturing processes and structural elements can be standardized, the resulting interposers are generally application-specific. GlobalFoundries will not be a TSMC supplier, but a subcontractor that will manufacture multiple customer-specific interposer designs rather than standardized components that require close cooperation with TSMC. Specifically, GlobalFoundries will need to ensure compatibility between its design rules, manufacturing processes, and qualification procedures so that interposers produced by GF can be used in TSMC's CoWoS packaging flows. It remains to be seen how the companies will handle ownership and protection of intellectual property, as interposer layouts may incorporate technologies and production methods specific to TSMC and its customers.By transferring some interposer production to GlobalFoundries, TSMC could free up some of its own manufacturing resources and increase availability of components required for advanced packaging.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsManufacturing silicon interposers is only one part of the CoWoS-S production process. The technology also requires attaching logic chiplets and HBM stacks to interposers using high-precision bonding equipment, assembling the resulting structures onto organic substrates, and then performing electrical testing. These operations require dedicated manufacturing capacity, which the agreement between the two companies does not address.Becoming a part of TSMC's CoWoS ecosystemFollowing its exit from development of leading-edge process technologies in 2018 and consequent inability to produce leading-edge AI and HPC accelerators, GlobalFoundries is now becoming a part of TSMC's advanced packaging supply chain in the U.S. that will supply custom components for AI and HPC processors.For GlobalFoundries, the agreement represents an opportunity to participate in the manufacturing of advanced AI processors without producing their leading-edge logic dies. Although the company abandoned the development of leading-edge process technologies eight years ago, its manufacturing capabilities remain suitable for producing certain components used in sophisticated multi-chip packages, including CoWoS-S interposers. It remains to be seen though whether it can also participate in TSMC's CoWoS-L supply chain. What to read next TSMC fab equipment demand nearly doubles in six months Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmaps — breaking down TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and GlobalFoundries' approach to next-generation scale-up connectivity New semiconductor firm, TYLsemi, breaks cover, backed by $43 million in early-stage funding The agreement with GlobalFoundries is particularly important considering TSMC's plans to establish advanced packaging operations in Arizona. The company intends to introduce CoWoS and 3D-IC packaging capabilities in the state before 2029 and has signed a 10-year agreement with Amkor Technology, which is building an advanced packaging facility in Peoria, Arizona, that is scheduled to begin production in early 2028.As GlobalFoundries ramps up interposer production in New York in the first half of 2028, TSMC could potentially establish a largely domestic CoWoS supply chain that comprises logic dies manufactured in Arizona, silicon interposers produced in New York, and advanced packaging and testing performed by TSMC and/or Amkor in Arizona. For a while, HBM stacks would still have to be sourced from memory manufacturers in Asia, though both Micron and SK hynix intend to bring HBM assembly facilities to the U.S. already this decade, so it is safe to say that the U.S. will have a vertically integrated supply chain for production of advanced AI processors by 2029 – 2030.There is a catch, though, as GloFo and TSMC have not disclosed how CoWoS assembly operations will be divided between TSMC and Amkor, or whether GlobalFoundries' interposers will be used in Arizona at all. Yet, GF's wording about a trusted U.S. manufacturing footprint strongly implies that its interposers will be primarily aimed at SiPs fabricated entirely in the U.S. Meanwhile, expanding interposer production alone will not increase the number of finished AI processors unless sufficient chip-on-wafer assembly and testing capacity is available.Some things remain unclearThe initial agreement covers five years and establishes a mechanism for further capacity additions. However, the companies have not disclosed the planned manufacturing volumes, capital expenditures associated with the expansion, or the breakdown of the $2 billion agreement. Furthermore, we yet have to find out how GF's manufacturing capabilities are aligned with CoWoS-S' advancements. history.titleZh: GlobalFoundries to produce silicon interposers for TSMC's CoWoS in the US — Five-year agreement valued at $2 billion
history.descriptionZh:
GlobalFoundries与台积电已签署一项为期五年、价值20亿美元的制造协议。根据协议，GlobalFoundries将在其纽约州马耳他（Malta）晶圆厂扩产，为台积电的CoWoS-S先进封装技术生产硅中介层（silicon interposer）。这是首次为CoWoS关键组件建立美国本土制造来源，使台积电客户能够将产品标注为“完全在美国制造并封装”。双方计划在2028年上半年开始量产，协议还建立了根据需求进一步扩产的框架，但未披露具体产能、资本支出以及20亿美元协议的分项构成。

背景方面，AI和高性能计算（HPC）对多芯片处理器的需求激增，台积电CoWoS先进封装产能长期紧张，成为AI加速器出货的瓶颈之一。台积电正计划在亚利桑那州建立先进封装能力，目标在2029年前引入CoWoS和3D-IC封装，并与Amkor签署十年协议，后者在亚利桑那州Peoria建设的先进封装厂预计2028年初投产。GlobalFoundries则在2018年退出前沿制程开发后，无法生产领先的AI/HPC逻辑芯片，但此次合作使其以成熟制造能力切入台积电的先进封装供应链，成为美国本土AI芯片封装生态的一部分。

核心技术原理在于，CoWoS-S封装通过硅中介层实现逻辑芯粒（chiplet）与高带宽内存（HBM）堆栈之间的高密度互连。中介层是定制化硅片，其配置取决于逻辑芯粒和HBM堆栈的数量、尺寸、位置及互连方式，同时必须满足特定处理器的供电需求，包括电源分配网络和嵌入式深沟槽电容（DTC），并兼顾信号完整性、电源完整性和热特性。由于大尺寸中介层可能超过光刻掩模版的最大曝光尺寸，需要采用拼接（stitching）工艺，因此GlobalFoundries能否为超大系统级封装（SiP）良好完成拼接仍有待观察。GlobalFoundries并非台积电的传统供应商，而是分包商，将为多个客户定制中介层设计，而非标准化组件。这要求其设计规则、制造工艺和认证流程与台积电CoWoS封装流程兼容，同时双方还需处理中介层版图中可能涉及台积电及其客户专有技术的知识产权归属和保护问题。

从产业影响看，将部分中介层生产转移给GlobalFoundries可释放台积电自身制造资源，提高先进封装所需组件的可用性。若与亚利桑那州生产的逻辑芯片、台积电和Amkor在亚利桑那的封装测试能力结合，美国有望形成本土CoWoS供应链：逻辑芯片在亚利桑那制造，硅中介层在纽约生产，封装和测试在亚利桑那完成。HBM堆栈短期内仍需从亚洲存储厂商采购，但Micron和SK海力士均计划在本十年内于美国建立HBM组装设施，因此到2029至2030年，美国可能拥有生产先进AI处理器的垂直整合供应链。不过，仍有许多细节不明：双方未说明CoWoS组装业务如何在台积电与Amkor之间分配，也未确认GlobalFoundries的中介层是否会用于亚利桑那工厂。制造硅中介层只是CoWoS-S流程的一部分，后续还需高精度键合设备将逻辑芯粒和HBM贴装到中介层、组装到有机基板并进行电测试，这些环节需要专门产能，而当前协议并未覆盖。仅扩大中介层生产并不足以增加成品AI处理器数量，除非芯片-on-晶圆组装和测试产能同步扩张。此外，GlobalFoundries能否参与更先进的CoWoS-L供应链、其制造能力如何与CoWoS-S技术演进保持对齐，也尚待观察。

总体而言，这项协议是美国半导体供应链本土化和AI先进封装格局重构的重要一步，旨在缓解CoWoS产能瓶颈并强化美国本土制造，但其实际效果取决于后续产能配套、良率、知识产权安排以及封装测试环节的协同扩张。

history.title: Finland orders Google to stop work on two AI data centers over alleged deforestation
history.description: Finnish authorities say they cannot conduct a proper environmental assessment after the site has already been changed.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Google subsidiary Tuike Finland Oy has just received a notice from the Finnish Licensing and Supervision Agency, or LVV, ordering it to stop construction on two data centers. According to CNBC, the sites in Muhos and Kajaani cannot proceed until environmental impact assessments have been completed, which have been under investigation for allegedly clearing over 740 acres of Finnish forest for the project.“We understand the concerns and have fallen short of our own high standards in this instance,” a Google spokesperson told the publication. “We acted in good faith under the Forestry Act and ran nature surveys and put in place measures to protect high-value areas. As we continue our long-term work in the region, we are advancing our landscaping and biodiversity plans, which include tree planting across 130 hectares at Muhos.”Finland is sometimes called the “Texas of Europe” when it comes to data centers because of its readily available supply of land and electricity, which have been some of the major bottlenecks that data center developers have been facing. Even though the epicenters of the AI data center infrastructure build-up are centered around the U.S. and China, Europe is trying to catch up with its massive $30 billion investment and a target of 100,000 AI GPUs for each site. SoftBank also plans to invest $87 billion specifically in France because of its nuclear-powered electricity grid.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: However, other European nations are struggling with the demand for this power-hungry infrastructure. Denmark has paused new data center connection requests as demand hit 60GW — more than eight times the country’s peak power consumption of around 7GW — while Amazon’s data center projects on the continent are facing delays of up to seven years as they wait for new connections.These stop-work orders aren’t related to electricity supply, though. Instead, the concerns stem from the alleged cutting of trees without the go-signal from the government. The LVV ordered the subsidiary to stop removing trees and topsoil, as well as cease activities such as excavation, quarrying, crushing, soil mass transfers, ditching, and road and storage construction. “In our opinion, the measures in question will change the environment and cause impacts, the identification and assessment of which are among the key objectives of the EIA procedure,” LVV environmental department head Tommi Muilu said in a statement. Still, the subsidiary can proceed with planning, measurement, soil surveys, and other activities that would only have minimal impacts. You may like Google AI data center project investigated after 420 football fields of Finnish forest demolished Microsoft-backed AI data center faces backlash over alleged unpermitted gas turbines and 1.5M-gallon LNG tank Amazon warns $68 billion in blocked data centers threatens US AI lead U.S. data centers have increasingly faced resistance from residents and communities around them, with 45 projects worth $68 billion blocked in the second quarter of 2026. We haven’t seen the same level of high-profile opposition in Europe, but this is likely because of the stricter permitting and review processes in the region, where concerns are usually raised and addressed even before construction begins. history.titleZh: 芬兰因涉嫌砍伐森林命令谷歌停止两个AI数据中心的工作
history.descriptionZh:
谷歌旗下子公司 Tuike Finland Oy 近日收到芬兰许可与监督机构 LVV 的停工令，要求其位于穆霍斯（Muhos）和卡亚尼（Kajaani）的两个数据中心项目暂停建设。根据 CNBC 报道，在完成环境影响评估（EIA）之前，这两个站点不得继续推进。相关调查针对该项目涉嫌为数据中心建设清理超过 740 英亩、约 300 公顷的芬兰森林。

LVV 的命令不仅要求停止砍伐树木和移除表土，还禁止挖掘、采石、破碎、大规模土方转移、开沟，以及道路和存储设施建设。LVV 环境部门负责人 Tommi Muilu 表示，这些措施将改变环境并造成影响，而识别和评估这些影响正是环境影响评估程序的核心目标。不过，该公司仍可继续进行规划、测量、土壤调查等影响较小的活动。

谷歌发言人对 CNBC 回应称：“我们理解相关担忧，并在这一事件中未达到自身的高标准。我们依据《森林法》诚信行事，开展了自然调查，并采取措施保护高价值区域。随着我们继续在该地区的长期工作，我们正在推进景观和生物多样性计划，包括在穆霍斯种植 130 公顷树木。” 这一回应显示，谷歌试图强调其环境修复和生物多样性承诺，但未能阻止监管机构发出停工令。

从背景看，这场争议并非直接源于电力供应，而是源于环境许可与森林保护问题。芬兰常被称为欧洲数据中心的“得克萨斯”，原因是其土地和电力供应相对充足，而这两者正是数据中心开发商面临的主要瓶颈。当前，AI 数据中心基础设施建设的中心仍在美国和中国，欧洲正试图以约 300 亿美元的投资追赶，并提出每个站点部署 10 万块 AI GPU 的目标。软银还计划在法国投资 870 亿美元，部分原因是法国拥有核电支撑的电网。

但欧洲其他国家正面临这种高耗能基础设施带来的压力。丹麦已暂停新的数据中心连接请求，因为需求达到 60GW，超过该国约 7GW 峰值用电量的八倍以上；亚马逊在欧洲的数据中心项目则因等待新电网连接而面临最长七年的延迟。这些数据表明，AI 数据中心不仅是芯片和服务器问题，更是电力、土地、冷却和环境许可的综合工程问题。

需要说明的是，原文并未涉及具体 AI 芯片架构、制程或算力创新，核心矛盾集中在数据中心基础设施的选址、供电与环境影响评估。AI 数据中心通常承载大规模 GPU/TPU 集群，用于 AI 训练、推理和云服务，其功率密度和冷却需求极高，因此对土地、电力、水资源和生态环境都有显著影响。环境影响评估程序的作用，就是在项目开工前识别土壤、植被、水文和生物多样性影响，并决定是否批准或如何修改建设方案。

与美国相比，欧洲目前尚未出现同等规模的高调反对浪潮，但这可能正是因为欧洲许可和审查流程更严格，许多问题在建设开始前就被提出和解决。美国在 2026 年第二季度已有 45 个、总价值 680 亿美元的数据中心项目受阻，显示社区和监管阻力正在成为 AI 基础设施扩张的重要变量。相关争议还包括谷歌 AI 数据中心项目被指毁坏约 420 个足球场面积的芬兰森林，以及微软支持的 AI 数据中心因涉嫌未经许可使用燃气轮机和 150 万加仑 LNG 储罐而遭到反对。

总体来看，这一事件反映 AI 算力扩张正从“芯片竞赛”延伸到“基础设施合规竞赛”。对谷歌而言，芬兰项目停工可能延迟其欧洲云与 AI 服务容量部署，增加成本和不确定性；对欧洲而言，则凸显在追求 AI 主权和算力自主的同时，必须平衡电力、土地、环境与社区接受度。芬兰的土地和电力优势仍然存在，但环保审查和生物多样性要求正在成为新的关键门槛。

history.title: Can you trust Meta’s Muse or OpenAI’s Dots to run your life?
history.description:
My Decoder guest today is Hayden Field, The Verge’s senior AI reporter, and we’re discussing the new wave of consumer-friendly AI agents. 
If you’ve been paying attention to this space, you know AI enthusiasts have been using agents for a minute now — homebrew OpenClaw setups led to a surge in Mac Mini sales earlier this year. But the launches of Meta’s Muse, OpenAI’s Dots, and xAI’s Grok Bot have brought easy-to-use agents to millions.
Muse and Dots have had the highest-profile product launches, and they’re fascinating to pit against each other. Both Meta and OpenAI have decided to pitch these agents to mainstream users and businesses in the form of cute animated mascots.
